The rate is a function of `D_target` and the hash only, never of the live true value, so it is a per-lie constant and restore-exact.
697	
698	**Example:** `arc_deg` 240, `needle_len_px` 24 (`rate_floor = max(0.5, 28.6 / 24) = 1.19`), `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC` 0.6, hash `H(1, 0x1234, 7, 0)` of D.14 (viewer 1, `ref_key` 0x1234, `start_run` 7): `h_rate mod 1001` = 61 gives `rate_draw = 0.5 + 1.5 x 0.061 = 0.59`; `h_mag mod 1001` = 566 gives `D_draw = 24 + 72 x 0.566 = 64.75 deg`.
699	
700	| Case | `L_s` | `rate_need` | `rate_nom` | `D_eff` | `t_arrive` |
701	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
702	| stage 1 GLIDE, short life | 40 s | 64.75 / (0.6 x 40) = 2.70 | clamp(max(0.59, 2.70), 1.19, 2.0) = **2.0** | min(64.75, 0.6 x 2.0 x 40 = 48) = **48 deg** | 24 s (0.60 `L_s`) |
703	| stage 2 GLIDE, mid life | 80 s | 1.35 | **1.35** | 64.75 | 48 s (0.60 `L_s`) |
704	| stage 3 GLIDE, long life | 120 s | 0.90 | max(0.59, 0.90) raised to `rate_floor` **1.19** | min(64.75, 85.8) = **64.75 deg** | 54.3 s (0.45 `L_s`) |
705	| stage 1 FALSE_OK, short life (*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*) | 40 s | 96 / (0.6 x 40) = 4.0 | clamp(4.0) = **2.0** | min(96, 48) = **48 deg** | 24 s |
706	| stage 2 FALSE_OK, mid life | 80 s | 96 / 48 = 2.0 | **2.0** | min(96, 96) = **96 deg** | 48 s |
707	| stage 3 FALSE_FAIL, long life | 120 s | 96 / 72 = 1.33 | **1.33** | min(96, 0.6 x 1.33 x 120 = 96) = **96 deg** | 72 s |
708	
709	The short-life row shows the reach rule working: a 64.75-deg draw would need 2.7 deg/s, so the departure is reduced to what 2.0 deg/s can do in `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC` of the life (counter `lies_partial` measures how often this happens; OQ-PF-10). Under reduced motion (`rm` 0.7) the six rows keep every `D_eff` and arrive at `D_eff / (0.7 x rate_nom)`: the three GLIDE rows at 34.3 s, 68.6 s and 77.6 s and the three FALSE rows at 34.3 s, 68.6 s and 102.9 s (each at 0.86 `L_s` or less; the hold before expiry is 5.7 s, 11.4 s and 42.4 s on the GLIDE rows and 5.7 s, 11.4 s and 17.1 s on the FALSE rows); no discrepancy is smaller, only later *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
710	
711	### D.3 Displayed value (the lie trajectory and the slew)
712	
713	The displayed value formula (registry: `lie_displayed_value`; covers D.1 to D.4) is defined as:
714	
715	`delta_pm(tau) = min(rate * tau, D_eff) * 1000 / arc_deg`
716	
717	`raw_pm(t) = u_true(t) + s * delta_pm(lie_tau)` for kind GLIDE
718	
719	`raw_pm(t) = u_true(t) + sgn(u_aim(t) - u_true(t)) * min(delta_pm(lie_tau), abs(u_aim(t) - u_true(t)))` for kinds FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL, with the aim point `u_aim(t) = clamp(u_true(t), z_lo + m_z, z_hi - m_z)` (the zone centre if the zone is narrower than `2 m_z`), `m_z = max(ZONE_MARGIN_PM, W_M)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
720	
721	`target_pm(t) = clamp(raw_pm(t), W_M, 1000 - W_M)` (the live dial clamp; `W_M` is the wander peak in pm)
722	
723	`slew_pm(t + dt) = clamp(slew_pm(t) + clamp(target_pm(t + dt) - slew_pm(t), -R_act * dt, +R_act * dt), u_true - DISC_CAP_PM, u_true + DISC_CAP_PM)`, `R_act = rm * GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG * 1000 / arc_deg`, `DISC_CAP_PM = D_MAX_FRAC_ARC * 1000`, `hard_start: slew_pm := clamp(target_pm, u_true - DISC_CAP_PM, u_true + DISC_CAP_PM)`
724	
725	`displayed_pm(t) = clamp(round(slew_pm(t) + w_pm(t)), 0, 1000)`, `displayed_value = value_lo + (value_hi - value_lo) * displayed_pm / 1000`
726	
727	**Variables:**
728	
729	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
730	|---|---|---|---|---|
731	| `u_true(t)` | float pm | [0, 1000] | the Filter's own read of `true_value` mapped through the calibration record (the Filter is the only non-diagnostic caller, LS-19) | the live true reading |
732	| `s` | int | {-1, +1} | the kind's side for FALSE_*; hash tag 8 for GLIDE, comfort-biased per `KIND_W` (Sanity-owned) | departure direction on the dial |
733	| `[z_lo, z_hi]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | float pm | within [0, 1000] | calibration record: the OK (FALSE_OK) or alarm (FALSE_FAIL) zone as an interval | the zone a FALSE_* needle is drawn into; success is the displayed interval `[displayed - W_M, displayed + W_M]` intersecting it |
734	| `W_M`, `m_z`, `ZONE_MARGIN_PM` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | float pm | `W_M` = `WANDER_AMP_PX x 1000 / (needle_len_px x arc_rad)` (21.9 pm at 24 px and 240 deg); `ZONE_MARGIN_PM` 20 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 10 to 50 | derived, Filter | the wander peak in pm (the target never leaves `[W_M, 1000 - W_M]`, so the displayed value plus the wander stays on the dial and the wander is never clamped away) and the margin by which the aim sits inside the zone |
735	| `DISC_CAP_PM` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | float pm | 400 at defaults | derived: `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000` | the largest displayed-minus-true the slew may hold: the 40 % fairness cap applied to the slew as well as the target |
736	| `rate`, `D_eff` | float | D.2 | D.2 | per-lie constants |
737	| `lie_tau` | float s | D.1 | D.1 | sim-time age since activation |
738	| `slew_pm` | float pm | [0, 1000] | **presentation-local state**, never persisted, one per ref | the rate-limited value that carries the lie and (D.6) the return |
739	| `R_act` | float pm/s | 8.33 at defaults | derived | the slew rate bound while ACTIVE; bounded by `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, **not** `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`; only the `DISC_CAP_PM` clamp may move the slew faster (a documented, bounded exception, OQ-PF-40) |
740	| `dt` | float s | 0 to `DT_SLEW_MAX_S` 0.1 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | frame delta on `present_time`, clamped | a render hitch cannot make the slew jump |
741	| `w_pm(t)` | float pm | D.4 | D.4 | wander, added **outside** the slew (its instantaneous speed would otherwise be clipped) |
742	| `value_lo`, `value_hi` | number | `value_lo` < `value_hi`, in the ref's unit | calibration record | the instrument's range in the ref's own unit (numerals, suit keys) |
743	
744	**Output Range:** `displayed_pm` is an integer in [0, 1000]. For GLIDE the discrepancy `displayed - true` is `s x delta` (monotone to `D_eff`, then held) plus the slew lag; for FALSE_* the needle departs toward the zone and holds the zone, so the discrepancy is `min(delta, d_aim)`, `d_aim` the aim distance *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `target_pm` is C0-continuous across both regimes and across a sign flip of `u_aim - u_true` (where the aim distance is 0). **Slew bound and the one exception** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the slew moves at no more than `R_act` except where the `DISC_CAP_PM` clamp binds, which happens only after a truth step larger than the cap minus the current offset or a truth ramp faster than `R_act` held long enough for the lag to reach the cap (5.5 s at a ramp of 100 pm/s from a +100 pm offset, see the example); there the slew is pinned `DISC_CAP_PM` from the truth and follows it. Without the clamp a breach that dropped the true reading by 600 pm would leave the lying needle up to a full dial (a minute at `R_act`) from the room, past the 40 % fairness cap, hiding exactly the emergency `W_MIN_WARNING_S` protects. A FALSE_OK that outlives a degrading truth keeps hiding it (a zone is a place on the dial, not an offset); a GLIDE cannot collapse or grow unseen between Sanity's 5 Hz re-checks (an offset is carried with the truth).
745	
746	**Restore and slew proof (the law is history-free).** (1) The formula `target_pm` is a pure function of `(lie_tau, u_true, per-lie constants)`. (2) `hard_start` sets `slew_pm := target_pm` (held within `DISC_CAP_PM` of the truth), so on the first frame after a restore or `force_stage` the displayed value equals the formula. (3) The slew is invisible whenever the target's per-frame change is within `R_act x dt`, which is always true for the formula itself (its own drift is at most `rate <= GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` and `R_act` is that bound). (4) The slew becomes visible only after a **step in the true value** (a Graph step, `apply_damage`) or a **lie hand-off** (a new lie starting while a return is in flight, E-PF-3); it then reconverges in at most `gap / R_act` seconds, at most `0.5 x 1000 / 8.33 = 60 s` for a half-dial step before the cap, and never leaves `DISC_CAP_PM` of the truth (so the worst lag is about `DISC_CAP_PM / R_act` = 48 s; typically a few seconds) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. (5) Therefore the pre-save and post-restore displayed values differ only by the slew gap that was still closing at the save, and the post-restore value is the formula's value from frame one. (6) Both laws re-converge deterministically within one bounded slew because the state is a single clamped follower of a pure target.
747	
748	**Example:** `arc_deg` 240 (24 deg = 100 pm), kind GLIDE, `rate` 1.19, `D_eff` 24 deg, `s` = +1, `u_true` 700 pm. At `lie_tau` 10 s: `delta = min(11.9, 24) x 1000 / 240 = 49.6 pm`, `target = 749.6`. At 20.2 s `delta = 100 pm`, `target = 800` and holds. At 25 s the true value steps to 650 (a repair): `target = 750` (the 100-pm offset is carried), `R_act = 2.0 x 1000 / 240 = 8.33 pm/s`, so the displayed needle follows down over `50 / 8.33 = 6.0 s` with no snap, and the discrepancy never collapses. FALSE_OK with the zone `[800, 1000]` and `W_M` 21.9 (so `m_z` 21.9 and `u_aim = clamp(u_true, 821.9, 978.1)`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: with `u_true` 650 the aim is 821.9, 171.9 pm away, inside `D_eff` 400 pm: the needle reaches 821.9 and holds, its band `[800, 843.8]` inside the zone; with `u_true` 400 the aim is 421.9 pm away, over the 400 pm cap: the needle stops at 800 and its band `[778.1, 821.9]` only touches the zone edge (a weak lie that Sanity's pre-draw gate should have refused); with `u_true` 350 it stops at 750, the band `[728.1, 771.9]` misses the zone, and `lies_zone_missed` increments. (The earlier example aimed at the zone centre 900 and stopped at 800 for a centre 900 away, which taught players only that violet does not mean wrong.) **Truth ramp, GLIDE offset 100 pm** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the truth rises 100 pm/s; the slew follows at 8.33 pm/s, so displayed-minus-true falls from +100 to -400 pm in `500 / 91.7` = 5.5 s and is then pinned at -400 pm (`DISC_CAP_PM`) while the slew follows the truth at 100 pm/s: bounded by the cap and continuous, a fast move the lie does not choose. **Dial stop:** `u_true` 950, `s` = +1, `delta` 100 pm, `W_M` 21.9: `raw` 1050 clamps to `target` 978.1, so the displayed-minus-true is 28.1 pm (6.7 deg, under `D_VIS_MIN_DEG`: `lie_short_reach`), the gleam, the sound and the full wander run, and a +100 repair that pins the truth at 1000 moves the target to 978.1 and the needle stays on the dial.

**L-D, direction (the table of record).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* Every lie has an *effective direction* computed at the accept from its kind and the subject's true state, stored on the ledger entry (`direction`) and re-derived every run: **COMFORT** (the display says the subject is healthier than it is), **ALARM** (the display says it is worse than it is). A lie whose display would equal the truth has no direction and is not a lie (INVALIDATED, EC-SN-38). Healthy means `hp >= HP_OK` 7000, DEGRADED means `HP_FAIL` 3000 < `hp` < `HP_OK`, FAILED means `hp <= HP_FAIL`. The rails that apply, by direction:

| Kind and surface | True state | Direction | L-C, L-L, L-I, L-A | L-W witness | L-S ceiling | L-G guard | L-2I credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FALSE_OK | DEGRADED or FAILED | COMFORT | yes | an active consequence-channel witness of the fault | yes | yes | a fixed gauge on the loop; the scanner (carried and equippable, see L-2I) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| GLIDE (drift toward the comfort side) | DEGRADED or FAILED | COMFORT | yes | as FALSE_OK | yes | yes | as FALSE_OK *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| SPRITE_SWAP to the healthier frame (a rotor spinning on a stopped machine; a housing shown whole when cracked; the glow frame lit on an unpowered housing) | stopped, cracked or unpowered (DEGRADED or FAILED) | COMFORT | yes | as FALSE_OK | yes | yes | as FALSE_OK *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
----
**PF-33. No clean frame.**
*Rule.* The first RUNNING frame after LOADING, and the first frame after any `force_stage` or `force_level`, is presented **already filtered**: envelopes are set to their targets (`hard_start`), lies are drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak from frame one, and `perceived` is answerable before the first RUNNING frame (Sanity rebuilds `sanity.perception` in `post_restore`, SN-23). No fade-in from clean. Glide and breath *phase* and the slew state may differ after restore; **while a lie is ACTIVE** its presence, kind, leak and displayed value (by PF-11) do not: the first frame shows the formula's value, which equals the pre-save value except for any slew gap that was still closing at the save (D.3), and a return in progress at the save is not restored (the entry had already left `sanity.perception`; E-PF-5). Counter `first_frame_filtered`.
*Why.* "One unfiltered frame would be a free oracle" (SN-23); AC-SL-124: "the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` must already be presented through the Perception Filter for the restored sanity level - the black hold covers any rebuild". This answers SL OQ-11 as co-owner with Sanity and the Pipeline. (orchestrator ruling R20.)

**PF-34. Unseen lies and no leak culling.**
*Rule.* A listed lie is drawn whenever its surface is on screen and lit; there is no "seat away" special case; its trajectory is a function of sim time and reappears at the correct point. At far zoom (the large field) level-of-detail may reduce amplitude *detail* (breath sampling rate only; the wander amplitude and frequency are never reduced, D.4), never remove a leak mode. Counts are bounded by `LIES_MAX`, not by the field, so zooming out multiplies nothing.
**PF-37. Presentation randomness.**
*Rule.* Every draw the Filter needs (glide rate and magnitude, wander frequencies and phases, breath cycle periods, tick jitter and mode, mode-drop choice) is a **pure integer hash** of `(viewer, ref_key, lie_key, epoch)` plus a per-use tag (D.14), with explicit 32-bit masking after every multiply and operand bounds that avoid dependence on GDScript integer overflow `[UNV]`. Never `rng_derive` (sim-only, KERN D.10, H9), never the global RNG, never `RandomNumberGenerator`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `lie_key` is Sanity's `start_run` for the lie, masked to 32 bits and forced non-zero: Sanity's entry carries no `lie_id` (OQ-PF-35), and `start_run` is in the saved ledger, so every per-lie draw is restore-exact. **`epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw**: the epoch is presentation-local and not saved (AC-PF-70), so a per-lie draw that depended on it would change on a restore. `epoch` is used only by the rim, bleed and outline breath envelopes, where it increments only while that effect's amplitude is 0, so a re-draw is invisible (D.14 table). Statistical quality (avalanche, modulo bias) is a test, not an assumption.
*Why.* Restore-exactness and reproducibility across platforms; precedent LO-19 (the pure integer hash for gutter timing). -> ADR candidate: a PRESENTATION-only stream. (orchestrator ruling R19.)

**PF-45. Dial calibration contract *(designed; PF-45 answered by IW-8, OQ-PF-29)*.**
*Rule.* To draw a lie the Filter needs, per corruptible dial or readout surface, a calibration record supplied by the owning scene through the tag: `arc_deg` (dial sweep), `needle_len_px`, the zone bands as intervals `[z_lo, z_hi]` of the per-mille reading (one for the OK zone, one for the alarm zone) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and `lsb` (the readout's least-significant unit). Without it the surface is honest (PF-44, `lie_unrenderable`), and the coverage lint (PF-6 vi) makes that a build failure for any kind listed in `lie_targets.json`. Instruments also owe: a pivoted needle as a **separate** sprite or slice, a `_msk` slice naming the glass and needle-edge regions the gleam uses, both honest state frames on one sheet page, and the honest settle applied only when `motion_mode` is HONEST. **Linear branch (K-5, OQ-IW-26).** A LINEAR surface (a tank sight-glass meniscus; Instruments IW-8 `gauge_kind` and D.11 `linear_position`) supplies `travel_px` in place of `arc_deg` and `needle_len_px`. The Filter runs D.2 to D.6 in per-mille space with the angular quantities replaced by Instruments' pixel band (cited, never re-valued here): rate floor `r_floor_pm_s = 1000 x LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS / travel_px`; rate ceiling `r_floor_pm_s x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG / GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG` (the dial band's ratio, 4); return rate `r_floor_pm_s x GLIDE_RETURN_RATE / GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG`, so D.6's assertion holds; smallest visible departure `D_vis_pm = 1000 x D_VIS_MIN_PX / travel_px`; magnitude cap `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` of the travel; eligibility `travel_px >= TRAVEL_MIN_PX`. The wander (D.4) moves the meniscus row by `WANDER_AMP_PX`. An ineligible LINEAR surface is not lied on (the honest path, `lie_unrenderable`) unless the ref also has a visible digit mechanism, whose TICK or STALE is then its motion mode (AC-PF-111) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
**Linear column of D.2 and D.3** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the four In-World Instruments constants the linear branch uses are `LINEAR_TRAVEL_PX` 50 (one size at MVP), `D_VIS_MIN_PX` 4, `LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS` 0.5 and `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` 40 (all Instruments-owned `[PLACEHOLDER]`, cited in the Cited table, never re-valued here). Every dial quantity that is not already a fraction maps through `arc_deg_ref` 240 (the dial reference of Instruments D.11): `x_pm = 1000 x x_deg / arc_deg_ref`.

| Quantity | Dial (240 deg, 24 px needle) | Linear, `travel_px` 40 | Linear, `travel_px` 50 | Linear form |
*Why.* The Filter works in per-mille dial space and cannot invent geometry; Sanity's `lie_targets.json` names module surfaces, not dials. Instruments (designed) answers it with IW-8 (`gauge_kind`, the calibration record) and IW-9 (`value_lo` / `value_hi` per quantity).

Now I want to revisit Sanity's core worry about blocker 1 — that exposing a full listing of every live lie would effectively hand the stage-2 own-cone fringe an oracle for detecting whether a lie exists anywhere on the ship.

One fix is to add an `away` flag so reach_lie_active only considers entries where away is false, which also touches the Filter's stage C logic and the lies ledger in the debug overlay, plus duplicate-entry rules like E-PF-6. The real question is whether Sanity's `sanity_view` surface should be extended with this `away` bool and list all active entries, versus keeping the current-compartment-only rule and adding a separate away_lies list — the former seems simpler but partially reverses an earlier G1 ruling.

This is a GAP that needs owner-side resolution: Sanity should keep its `reach_lie_active`/stage semantics but broaden "listed" to mean every active entry tagged with `away`, since listing away entries stays OWNER_PRIVATE and local-seat-only so it isn't an information leak in co-op, and visibility through lit doors/surfaces is unaffected since the Filter only draws on-screen content. I'm now questioning whether the Filter actually needs the `away` flag at all, since it draws identically regardless.

The flag is only needed so the `reach_lie_active` predicate can exclude away entries while keeping them listed — I could instead publish that as a bool field directly in the seat record, but keeping the simple `away` flag and letting the Filter check tier, away-status, and active-state together is cleaner. This also fixes a side issue: previously an away lie's sound would cut off via RETURN→OFF when a seat left a compartment, creating an unwanted signature, but now the sound persists correctly regardless of visibility, and the rule that an entry's disappearance is the only true end-signal still holds.

I'm also checking edge cases: seat death/restore rebuilds entries identically, lies pending while away now correctly onset even off-screen without visible animation issues, and debunking still requires physical presence regardless of away status. #### S3. Lie presentation (per viewer, per `lie_id`)

| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NONE` | no entry for the ref and no RETURN in progress, or CLEAR reached after a return (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | entry appears ACTIVE -> `ONSET` | Sanity (entry appears in `sanity.perception`, SN-16) |
| `ONSET` | entry ACTIVE and the departure not complete (`lie_tau` below arrival time) | departure complete -> `HOLD`; entry removed early -> `RETURN` (the follower starts from the in-flight discrepancy) | Sanity (removal: expiry, a falsification, an invalidating re-check, a class disable); sim time (arrival) |
| `HOLD` | entry ACTIVE and arrived | entry removed -> `RETURN` | Sanity |
| `RETURN` | entry absent and CLEAR not yet reached (CLEAR is the later of discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, gleam amplitude 0 and wander faded to 0; `lie_id` and `lie_kind` stay non-zero throughout; the return is the slew state of PF-13 with the live true value as its target, rate `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | CLEAR -> `NONE`; a new entry on the same ref -> `ONSET` **from its own formula** (discrepancy 0 at `lie_tau` 0); the slew closes the gap from the in-flight value at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, no snap (E-PF-3) | the follower at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (presentation); Sanity (a new entry) |

`ONSET` and `HOLD` are both `motion_mode` GLIDE (or TICK or STALE for a readout, or BREATH for a static-pair frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); `RETURN` is `motion_mode` RETURN until CLEAR. SPRITE_SWAP uses the same four states with the gleam-leads-cut onset and the type-split return of PF-19. The leak amplitude follows PF-15 in every state; a stage change never moves the machine.

- **If a save is loaded, or LOADING happens, while a lie is in RETURN** *(E-PF-5)*: the return track is presentation-local and is dropped; the entry had already left `sanity.perception`, so nothing is ACTIVE, and the first RUNNING frame (behind the black hold) shows the true value. This is not a clean-frame oracle (no lie is active to hide). The residual tell, "loading cleared the tail", is accepted (OQ-PF-9 answered: ended entries are not retained, loading clears the tail).
- **If the subject of a lie is destroyed mid-glide (`true_value` no longer resolves)** *(E-PF-9)*: the entry leaves (INVALIDATED); the ref draws nothing (the instrument is gone), there is no return animation, and the per-lie state is freed the same frame. A Filter datum that throws or goes missing falls back to truth (PF-44).
### Zoom, geometry and the camera

- **If the zoom ladder changes step while a lie is ACTIVE** *(E-PF-27)*: the zoom is a cut (PIPE C6); `displayed_pm` is unchanged (it is in dial space); fringe and gleam widths are re-derived as `n x k'` on the first frame of the new rung and never interpolated; no leak mode is removed.
- **If the field is the largest (zoom 1x on 2160p, 3840x2160 art px, 36 times the default area)** *(E-PF-28)*: every on-screen lie is still drawn with every mode; level-of-detail may reduce amplitude detail (breath sampling rate only; the wander amplitude and frequency are never reduced, D.4), never remove a mode (a culled leak is an unleaked lie, PF-34); the draw count stays bounded by `LIES_MAX`, not the field (D.12).
- **If the window moves to a monitor of a different size so `k_auto` changes** *(E-PF-29)*: the ladder top moves (`k_auto + 2`), widths re-derive as in E-PF-27, and the smallest-region flash bound is re-evaluated at the new field (the flash scan covers the largest field).
- **If a lying surface is on screen but its host is unlit** *(E-PF-30)*: no gleam is drawn (the gleam rides the host's lit draw, PF-16), no prompt appears (IA-13) and the lie clock still runs; the Filter makes no `lit(ref)` query. An unlit gleam would be a location oracle and a phantom in the dark.
- **If a lying surface is off screen** *(E-PF-31)*: nothing is drawn and no shader work is done; because the trajectory is a function of sim time it reappears at the correct point of its glide, with no onset animation (PF-34).

- **AC-PF-66 (auto) [MVP-live]**: GIVEN a lying surface off screen for 50 s WHEN it returns on screen THEN its displayed value and leak equal the formula at the current `lie_tau`, with no onset animation. `[PF-34, E-PF-31]`
- **AC-PF-67 (auto) [MVP-live]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: GIVEN the largest field (3840x2160 at 1x, about 80 x 45 tiles at `TILE_PX` 48) WHEN a lie is 30 tiles (on screen), 60 tiles and 90 tiles (off screen) from the viewer THEN at each distance `leak_modes` is unchanged (GLEAM, the motion mode and SOUND all present), `amp` is at least `floor_eff` (never dimmed toward 0), the wander amplitude is 2.2 px and the sound request stays ON; the 60- and 90-tile lies advance on sim time, and when the viewer reaches them the displayed value equals the formula at the current `lie_tau` within the slew gap. `[PF-34, E-PF-28]`
- **AC-PF-68 (auto) [MVP-live]**: GIVEN PAUSED for 30 s WHEN frames are compared THEN `displayed_pm`, `amp`, breath phase, envelopes and the digit are unchanged, and the paused frame contains every active leak. `[S1, E-PF-24]`

918	### D.9 Lying-digit tick schedule
919	
920	The lying-digit tick formula is defined as:
921	
922	`T_tick = max(LIE_TICK_MS, N_r * 334)`
923	
924	`t_k = k * T_tick + j * T_tick / N_r` on `present_time`, `j` the readout's stagger index (ordered by hash tag 6); the stagger spacing `T_tick / N_r` is never below 334 ms, the single-readout floor
925	
926	`q_k = clamp(round(slew_value(t_k) / lsb), q_lo, q_hi)`, `q_lo = round(value_lo / lsb)`, `q_hi = round(value_hi / lsb)`; in TICK mode, if `q_k == q_{k-1}`, `q_k = q_{k-1} + sgn_k` (one `lsb`, sign from hash tag 6, flipped if it would leave `[q_lo, q_hi]`), so the digit changes every tick; in STALE mode `q_k` follows the **displayed** needle value by ticks while the lie is in ONSET and is **held from arrival** (when `delta_pm` reaches its aim), never the zone centre while the needle is still short of it, so the digit does not change while the ship changes. During RETURN the numeral keeps the TICK rule on the returning `slew_value` and switches to the honest grid at CLEAR (PF-18). A region gap governor defers any lying tick due less than 334 ms after the previous lying tick in the region; it never defers an honest swap, and the lying-to-honest switch lands on the next HUD grid boundary (PF-18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

928	**Variables:**

930	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
931	|---|---|---|---|---|
932	| `LIE_TICK_MS` | int ms | 400 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 334 to 1000; registered | Filter | single-readout interval. The **floor is 334 ms**: 333 ms is 3.003 transitions per second against AC-SN-149 "no more than 3 per second" |
933	| `N_r` | int | 1 to `LIES_MAX` (4, cited, Sanity) | derived | lying readouts in the same ninth of the displayed picture, counting HUD-layer readouts |
934	| `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` | int | 3 (cited, Pipeline) | registry | transition ceiling |

Without the scheduler four readouts at 400 ms would make 10 transitions per second, 3.3 times the ceiling. At `N_r` 4 the continuous cadence falls to 0.75 Hz: still never stopped, still distinguishable from an honest numeral (which changes on the HUD-owned `HONEST_TICK_MS` hold grid), but weaker (risk in Open Questions). Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): a flash event is one opposing pair of luminance transitions, so the counting unit is `flash_events = ceil(n_transitions / 2)` over a rolling second (the registry's `flash_count`), and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` is weighted per area with the creative-director exemptions (sub-threshold digit swaps and prompt show-starts exempt; the strict ceiling kept for the Alarm Red mark and under reduce-flashing, which defaults ON at first launch, X10). 1069

I'm questioning whether readout_mode is strictly tied to kind, since PF-18 expects TICK for GLIDE and STALE for FALSE_* states. There's a potential mismatch if Sanity were to publish TICK on a FALSE_OK case, and I need to check how the Filter would handle that conformance gap.

Resolving this, I conclude readout_mode should be kind-derived (GLIDE→TICK, FALSE_OK/FALSE_FAIL→STALE) as a pure function with no draw consumption, since Sanity's RNG draws are fixed at 4 per accepted onset and a derived mode avoids introducing extra randomness. This should be flagged as a clarification to add to SN-23's params row rather than a true conflict.

I'm also checking surface renames (HOUSING→GLOW_SPRITE, MACHINE→MACHINE_SPRITE) and confirming direction consistency for FALSE_OK/FALSE_FAIL cases, where mismatches between kind and direction should trigger debug assertions but release builds trust the published kind.

For the GLIDE sign calculation, I'm working out that it needs the orientation between the OK and alarm zone centers from calibration, and deciding that any record missing either zone interval should be treated as ineligible for GLIDE and fall back to lie_unrenderable per PF-44/45.

Then I'm considering whether the drift direction is fixed at acceptance or re-derived each run — if truth changes (e.g., a repair makes the system healthy while a GLIDE comfort lie is still live), the direction could flip or invalidate, which ties back to the rule that a lie whose display equals truth has no direction and isn't a lie at all.

So I'm settling on: the filter latches direction from the entry's stored value at the moment of acceptance, which stays immutable for that lie_id — if a re-derive ever produces a different direction mid-lie, that's treated as invalidation rather than a flip, since slew limiting wouldn't tolerate jumps anyway.

Now I'm thinking through how this affects the dial-room gate: with direction fixed, the room-check needs to evaluate the wander margin specifically on the side indicated by direction times comfort_sign, so the gate logic should reference that signed direction rather than assuming symmetry.

I should add a safety requirement tied to the blocker: for every GLIDE lie fixture, the sign of the displayed-minus-true offset must match the direction derived from the ledger after onset, verified via property test, plus a lint rule to catch violations.

I also need to retire hash tag 8 for direction but keep its vector reserved in hash_vectors.json for numbering stability, since tag numbers shouldn't be reused. And I need to fix PF-13's claim that direction is comfort-biased by KIND_W — it should state that direction belongs to Sanity, with Sanity picking the kind and the side following from the kind (FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL implying it).

- **Lifecycle.** PENDING (accepted, invisible for the delay so the activation can re-validate SN-15) to ACTIVE (in `sanity.perception`) to one of EXPIRED (`end_run` reached: the time rung), DEBUNKED (`record_falsification` only, SN-17; a PENDING lie can be DEBUNKED too), INVALIDATED (a guard rail no longer holds, the subject is destroyed or its `subject_ref` no longer resolves, the true state now equals the displayed state or the derived `direction` no longer equals the stored one). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: the reveal-by-full-channel cause is deleted from DEBUNKED, since a repair or inspect completion calls nothing (SN-17); the class-switched-off cause is deleted from INVALIDATED, since SN-28 says a class switched off lets live lies **expire normally** with no new onsets (no uncaused vanish); and PENDING to DEBUNKED is added to the transition table.)* All three end types leave `sanity.perception` on the same run and none is announced: the Filter returns the displayed value to the truth on the glide path at its `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (registry; never a snap, never a settle) with the leak amplitude following the remaining displayed-minus-true discrepancy, identically for EXPIRED, INVALIDATED and DEBUNKED, so the end type is never an oracle (ART 7.3, SNV-11, AD-C2). The lie's clock runs in sim time: if the seat leaves the compartment the clock keeps running and an unexpired lie is drawn again on return from its remaining life; a witness that ends before `end_run` (the fault was repaired) collapses the lie at the next run. **A stage change never ends a lie**: existing lies run to expiry and only new onsets use the new stage's caps and reach (a lie that vanishes exactly at a stage boundary is a tell of the boundary and uncaused pixel motion). *(Orchestrator ruling: SD proposed invalidating on a stage drop, GD keeping; keeping is adopted.)*

#### C. Stage, fringes and the container

**PF-21. Stage presentation: weather.**
*Rule.* The SIM stage steps instantly; the picture does not. Each stage-bound effect has a 0-to-1 **envelope** that slews linearly toward its target (`GAIN_e[stage] / 1000`) so that **every transition takes exactly `STAGE_RAMP_S`** of `present_time`: the rate is latched at each target change as the remaining distance over `STAGE_RAMP_S`, never above `1 / STAGE_RAMP_S` per second (D.7): `STAGE_RAMP_S` `[PLACEHOLDER]` default 8 s, range 6.5 to 20, registered, with the build assertion `STAGE_RAMP_S >= the breath period upper bound (6000 ms, ART 5.5) + a 0.5 s margin` (so 6.5 s; D.7, D.11). Amplitude-monotone, never a pulse, never announced, never an overshoot. So Sanity (owner) adds a bool `away` and lists every ACTIVE entry; away entries and tier-3 entries are excluded from `reach_lie_active`, which keeps SN-23's rim-oracle reason intact. Blocker 2 is four CONFLICTs resolved for the publisher (G1): `lie_key` := Sanity's `lie_id` (the vectors are unchanged, only relabelled from start_run 7 to lie_id 7); the join is the pair {stable_id, surface} with `quantity` moved into the PerceptionRef constructor; GLIDE side = `d x c_dial` from `direction` plus the calibration zones (hash tag 8 retired but its vector kept; new AC-PF-120); numeral mode from `params.readout_mode` or the kind map (new AC-PF-121).
